summary: Reviewed 4 modified files: mcp_parse.py (new), nodes/__init__.py (stage lifecycle events), supervisor.py (import refactor), test_nodes.py (new test classes).
All 9 acceptance criteria met. Architecture is clean and follows existing project conventions.
parse_tool_response extraction is a correct SRP refactor — supervisor and nodes now share the parser without duplication.
stage_start/stage_complete/stage_error lifecycle events are well-structured; timestamp capture precedes the try block ensuring accurate duration_s on both success and error paths.

pipeline_result uses wrapped_tools (already project-path-injected) and redundantly passes project_path explicitly — functionally correct since inject_project_path preserves explicit values.

comments.note: Dev dependencies pytest-asyncio, aiosqlite, and langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite are not declared in pyproject.toml dev extras. Tests silently produce confusing errors ('async functions are not natively supported' / ModuleNotFoundError) without them. Add to pyproject.toml [dev] extras to ensure reproducible test environments. Flagged by both Developer and QA.

parse_tool_response in mcp_parse.py has 4 distinct parsing branches (list-of-content-blocks, JSON string, ToolMessage-like, direct dict/other) but no dedicated unit tests. Currently exercised indirectly through supervisor and node integration tests. Isolated parametrized unit tests for each branch would make the contract explicit and catch regressions faster.

In nodes/__init__.py create_stage_node, state.get('current_wp_id', '') is called 4 separate times (start_entry, log_entry/stage_complete, wp_id local var, log_entry/stage_error). The value is immutable within the node invocation — capturing it once at the top of node_fn (e.g. `_wp_id = state.get('current_wp_id', '')`) would eliminate the duplication and the repeated type-ignore comments.

In the pipeline_result read-back block, get_wp_tool.ainvoke({'work_package_id': wp_id, 'project_path': project_path}) explicitly passes project_path even though get_wp_tool was obtained from wrapped_tools (which already injects project_path into calls that omit it). The explicit pass is harmless (inject_project_path preserves explicit values) but is redundant. Could drop project_path from the ainvoke call to keep the intent clear that wrapped_tools handles injection.
